subject: dsa
title: House Robber II
summary: The houses form a circle, so the first and last are adjacent and can't both be robbed. Run the plain House Robber line solution twice — once without the last house, once without the first — and take the larger result.
problem: Houses are arranged in a circle, so the first and last are adjacent. Rob the maximum total without robbing two adjacent houses.

steps.caption: The houses form a circle, so the first and last are neighbors — you can't rob both. Trick: solve the line version twice, dropping one end each time.
Case A: ignore the last house. Find the best non-adjacent haul in houses 0 through 2.
In [1, 2, 3], the best is house 0 plus house 2 = 1 + 3 = 4.
Case B: ignore the first house. Find the best non-adjacent haul in houses 1 through 3.
In [2, 3, 1], the best is 3 — take the 3 alone, or the 2 and 1 (also 3).
Answer = max(Case A, Case B) = max(4, 3) = 4, robbing house 0 and house 2.
